 #   --context-file <path>     Reviewer findings (review only; omit for audit independence)
 #   --model <model>           Dissenter model (default: from config or gpt-5.3-codex)
 #   --budget <cents>          Max cost in cents (default: from config or 150)
+#                             cycle-131 FR-4: flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale: fixed | diff
+#                             (default fixed — an absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged) and budget_cents_max
+#                             (default 600). diff: the gate's budget is min(max(<this budget>, ceil(estimate × 1.2)),

+# Findings (cycle-131 FR-4): each finding may carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end (the head-file line, or range, it
+# sits on) beside the symbol anchor; kept only as whole numbers 1..10,000,000 (end ≥ start), else dropped silently.
 #   --timeout <seconds>       API timeout (default: from config or 60)
 #   --dry-run                 Assemble context without calling API
 #   --json                    Output as JSON (default)
@@ -145,6 +155,49 @@ _conf_uint() {  # <key (for the message)> <raw> <default> [floor] → a whole nu
   echo "$def"
 }
 
+# cycle-131 FR-4 (SDD D-4.2): flatline_protocol.<gate>.budget_scale (fixed | diff, default fixed) and
+# flatline_protocol.<gate>.budget_cents_max (default 600). Fails CLOSED to `fixed`: a scale that is not one of the two words

+#   Citation validity first (both clauses of the new rule): a cited line is positive;
+#   a cited range is ordered (a <= b, the parser orders it); when the defect's file
+#   exists under the head directory the range must lie inside it (1 <= a <= b <= its

+#   validity rule, no range cap), so recall_pm3_v1 reproduces a 1.2.x grade.
+#   Detection: a valid citation (path, a, b) detects defect d when its path matches d's
+#   file and (i) [a, b] lies within ±3 of any site (unchanged), OR (ii) same scope: the
+#   enclosing definition of the site in head/<file>, identified by its HEADER LINE

+#   [a, b]. Definition headers: bash (.sh, .bash, or a bash/sh shebang)

+#   `^\s*def NAME\(`; bats `^@test "…"` plus the bash forms; markdown `#` headings

+#   the line before the next header at the same or lower indentation (markdown: the
+#   same or a higher heading level), else to the end of the file, and no further than
+#   its own end (end-of-definition detection): bash and bats — the first `}` line at
+#   the header's indentation (a one-line `f() { …; }` ends on its header); python —
+#   the last line before the first later non-blank, non-comment line indented no
+#   deeper than the def. Nested definitions resolve to the innermost (the latest

+#   before the next header is top-level.
+#   Caps: a definition longer than 400 lines, or a file type with no definition
+#   regex (yaml, json, txt, tsv, …), falls back to ±20 lines around the site (and a
+#   cited line in such a definition has no scope); a site outside every definition
+#   (top-level code, text before the first heading) has no scope (±3 only).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# recall-vs-defects.sh — deterministic planted-defect recall grader
#
# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9). Args: $1=workspace, $2=fixture id (pr-NN),
# $3=review file (default review.md). Reads the HIDDEN manifest
# evals/fixtures/review-prs/manifests/<id>.json (never copied into the
# sandbox) and the agent's review.
#
# Rule (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol, no fuzzy adjudication): a defect is DETECTED
# when the review contains a `path:line` (or `path:line-line`) citation whose
# path ends with the defect's file (repo-relative, `head/`-prefixed, or the
# bare basename) and whose line, or line range, falls within ±3 of the
# manifest anchor — `anchor_line`, or any line in `anchors[]` for a defect
# with more than one site.
#
# Parser (1.1.0, bd-ewrc): a leading `(` is not part of the path; comma
# continuations (`path:776,807`, `path:10, 118-121`) and a later bare `:N` or
# `head:N` / `base:N` bind to the most recent cited path. A `:N` glued to a
# word or a number (`note:40`, `10:40`), or with no cited path before it,
# credits nothing.
#
# Parser 1.1.1 (sprint-250 review run 1, n40-n42): the LOA-VERDICT trailer is
# removed before citations are parsed, and a bare `:N` after a quote, bracket,
# brace or `*` (JSON such as `"high":3`) credits nothing; a backtick- or
# bold-wrapped path (`` `b.sh`:40 ``, `**b.sh**:40`) binds its own line; a comma
# continuation or range stays on its line, and a continuation must end at a
# number boundary (no dates);
# a path containing `//` (a URL) is not a citation.
# Run 2 (#11/#13-#15): a match inside any URL token (`scheme://...`) is not a
# citation; a range dash is unspaced and every number (first, continuation,
# bare) ends at a boundary (no further `-N` / `–N`: no dates); the
# quote/bracket guard applies only to the fully bare `:N` (plus a closing
# backtick), so `"head:40"` binds as in 1.1.0; one trailer pattern strips and
# reads the LOA-VERDICT comment and never crosses another comment's bounds.
# Parser 1.1.2 (the run 2 changes above, plus sprint-250 review run 3): the
# URL look-back takes the text after the last whitespace — one linear split —
# so a citation that opens a line never inherits the previous line's URL.
# The parser runs as `python3 -I -` (audit dissent run 1, n32): a module planted
# in the invoker's cwd (a forging json.py) is never imported (RG-27).
#
# Grader 1.2.0 (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.3): adds the refuted-share figure;
# the recall rule and the pass/score contract are unchanged. A FINDING is one
# distinct cited (path, line-range); it is MATCHED when it overlaps (±3) a
# defect site or a manifest `fix_regions[]` entry ({file, start, end}: the
# head-side lines a record fixture's fix commit touched). details gain
# findings_cited, findings_refuted and refuted_share (refuted / cited; null
# when nothing is cited).
#
# Clean fixtures (0 planted defects) measure FALSE POSITIVES: the LOA-VERDICT
# trailer's critical+high counts; without a trailer, every file:line citation
# counts as one.
#
# Output: {"pass", "score", "details":{recall, planted, detected[], missed[],
#          false_positives, severity_counts, model, effort, tokens}, "grader_version"}
#   pass  = every planted defect detected (defect fixture) / zero false
#           positives (clean fixture); score = recall*100 or 100/0.
# Exit: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 error (missing manifest / bad args)
#
# Tested by evals/tests/eval-recall-grader.bats.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

workspace="${1:-}"
fixture="${2:-}"
review_name="${3:-review.md}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
MANIFEST_DIR="${EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../fixtures/review-prs/manifests}"

err() { printf '{"pass":false,"score":0,"details":{"error":%s},"grader_version":"1.2.0"}\n' "$(jq -Rn --arg m "$1" '$m')"; exit 2; }

[[ -n "$workspace" && -d "$workspace" ]] || err "invalid workspace"
[[ -n "$fixture" && "$fixture" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || err "invalid fixture id"
manifest="$MANIFEST_DIR/$fixture.json"
[[ -f "$manifest" ]] || err "manifest not found: $manifest"
case "$review_name" in */*|..*) err "review file must be a bare name" ;; esac

review="$workspace/$review_name"
executor="$workspace/.eval/executor.json"

import json, os, re, stat, sys
manifest_path, review_path, executor_path, manifest_v1_path, head_dir = sys.argv[1:6]
man = json.load(open(manifest_path))
man_v1 = json.load(open(manifest_v1_path)) if manifest_v1_path else man
text = open(review_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()

# path:line[-line] citations. Path = something with a file extension; the
# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
CITE = re.compile(
    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
ONE = re.compile(RNG)
cites = []
last = None
# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
for m in CITE.finditer(body):
    if m.group("path") is not None:
        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
            continue
        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
        if p.startswith("./"):
            p = p[2:]
        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
    elif last is not None:
        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
    else:
        continue
    for r in ONE.finditer(spans):
        a = int(r.group(1)); b = int(r.group(2)) if r.group(2) else a
        if b < a:
            a, b = b, a
        cites.append((p, a, b))

def path_matches(cited, defect_file):
    cited = cited.split("head/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("head/") else cited
    cited = cited.split("base/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("base/") else cited
    if cited == defect_file or defect_file.endswith("/" + cited):
        return True
    return cited == defect_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

# ---- 1.3.0: head files, definition scopes, citation validity --------------------------
RANGE_CAP = 25      # a wider cited range credits only through its first line
SPAN_CAP = 400      # a longer definition falls back to ±FALLBACK around the site
FALLBACK = 20
BASH_HDR = (re.compile(r'^(\s*)(?:function\s+)?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*\s*\(\)\s*\{?'),
----
det_pm3, mis_pm3 = split(man, hit_pm3)
detected, missed = split(man, hit_new)
function_only = [x for x in detected if x not in det_pm3]

planted = len(man.get("defects", []))
recall = rate(detected, man)

# refuted share (1.2.0): distinct cited findings that touch no defect site and
# no fix region. Regions are (file, lo, hi) on head/ line numbers, widened ±3.
regions = []
for d in man.get("defects", []):
    for s in (d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]):
        regions.append((d["file"], s - 3, s + 3))
for fr in man.get("fix_regions", []) or []:
    try:
        regions.append((fr["file"], int(fr["start"]) - 3, int(fr["end"]) + 3))
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        continue

refuted = [c for c in findings
           if not any(path_matches(c[0], f) and not (c[2] < lo or c[1] > hi) for f, lo, hi in regions)]
refuted_share = round(len(refuted) / len(findings), 4) if findings else None

# trailer → severity counts (false positives on clean fixtures)
sev = None
tm = TRAILER.search(text)
if tm:
    try:
        sev = json.loads(tm.group(1)).get("counts")
    except Exception:
        sev = None
if isinstance(sev, dict):
    fp = int(sev.get("critical", 0) or 0) + int(sev.get("high", 0) or 0)
else:
    fp = len({(p, a, b) for p, a, b in cites})
false_positives = fp if planted == 0 else 0

model = effort = None
tokens = None
try:
    ex = json.load(open(executor_path))
    model, effort = ex.get("model_id"), ex.get("effort")
    u = ex.get("usage") or {}
    # every token the call consumed: uncached input, cache writes, cache
    # reads and output — the prompt surface is mostly CACHED input, so
    # input_tokens alone (30 on a real run) would hide the very thing the
    # prompt diet changes
    tokens = sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
                 ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
except Exception:
    pass

if planted:
    ok = len(missed) == 0
    score = int(round(recall * 100))
else:
    ok = false_positives == 0
    score = 100 if ok else 0

out = {
    "pass": ok,
    "score": score,
    "details": {
        "recall": recall, "planted": planted, "detected": detected, "missed": missed,
        "recall_pm3": rate(det_pm3, man), "detected_pm3": det_pm3, "missed_pm3": mis_pm3,
        "recall_pm3_v1": rate(det_v1, man_v1), "detected_pm3_v1": det_v1, "missed_pm3_v1": mis_v1,
        "planted_v1": len(man_v1.get("defects", [])), "v1_manifest": bool(manifest_v1_path),
        "credits_function_only": function_only, "rule": "pm3_or_same_function",
        "false_positives": false_positives, "severity_counts": sev,
        "citations": len(cites), "model": model, "effort": effort, "tokens": tokens,
        "findings_cited": len(findings), "findings_refuted": len(refuted),
        "refuted_share": refuted_share,
    },
    "grader_version": "1.3.0",
}
print(json.dumps(out))
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

+def expand(tok, vars_):

+def classify(tok, cwd, ws):

+def sections(text, targets):

+    a line that is not diff body and names a file (an `echo "=== $f"` marker); a header naming a target
+    (the longest one it holds) opens that target's section, any other header a dropped one; text before
+    the first header belongs to the sole target. Text no header attributes (several targets) is returned
+    as the loose list. Header lines are not part of a body. → (sections, loose)"""
+    out = {f: [] for f in targets}
+    loose = []
+    cur = targets[0] if len(targets) == 1 else None
+    buf = []
+
+    def flush():
+        if buf:
+            (out[cur] if cur is not None else loose).append("\n".join(buf))
+
+    for line in text.split("\n"):
+        diff_hdr = line.startswith(("diff ", "--- ", "*** ", "+++ "))
+        if diff_hdr or (not DIFF_BODY.match(line) and FILEISH.search(line)):

+            hit = named[0] if named else None
+            if line.startswith("+++ ") and hit == cur:
+                continue
+            if hit is not None or diff_hdr or len(targets) > 1:
+                flush()
+                buf = []
+                cur = hit
+                continue
+        buf.append(line)
+    flush()
+    return out, loose

+def oracle_plan(tool, inp, ws, answer):
+    """[(how, answer path)] a tool_use could expose: diff or read; [] when it names no answer path"""

+            if c and c[0] == "ws":
+                out += [("read", f) for f in ws_targets(c[1], answer, tool == "Grep")]
+        return out

+        return out

+def plan_sides(plan, f):

+    return tuple(sorted(sides))

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Closed mount for review-catch sandboxes (cycle-131 FR-1, SDD §5.2, D-1.1/D-1.2,
+# DEC-0613 as amended by DEC-0622, DEC-0615). One Python core serves the overlay,
+# the pre-launch check (check_mount_closed) and took-effect.sh's oracle_closed rule,
+# so the launched surface and the post-run verdict use the same comparison.
+#
+# _sm_oracle_py answer-set <fixture-dir> <source-repo>
+#     prints "<pr|fix>\t<path>" per answer-bearing path (sorted)
+# _sm_oracle_py overlay <ws> <fixture-dir> <mode> <source-repo>
+#     applies the overlay; prints the evidence key=value lines on stdout, notes on stderr
+# _sm_oracle_py check <ws> <fixture-dir> <evidence-file> <source-repo> <source-commit>
+#     clauses (a)-(d); exit 0 with "ok …", exit 1 with "FAIL (<clause>) <path>: <detail>"

+# Answer-bearing set (computed from the IMMUTABLE fixture, never the sandbox pr/):
+#   (i) every path named by head.diff: `diff --git` headers (C-quoted paths unquoted,

+#       (both names), ---/+++ lines outside hunks (/dev/null skipped, a trailing tab
+#       stripped), "Binary files … differ" lines; CRLF tolerated; hunk bodies are
+#       skipped by their line counts so a removed "-- a/x" line is never a header;
+#   (ii) every file or symlink under <fixture>/head/ and <fixture>/base/;
+#   (iii) the fixture.yaml fix_commit's paths (git show --no-renames --name-only):

+#   regular file there (deleted, added in base mode, a symlink, a symlink component,
+#   unknown head commit) → the path is removed from the mount and expected absent.
+#   The file mode's executable bit is kept (fixture file mode / tree entry mode).
+# Sandbox writes never follow a symlink: an existing symlink at the path is unlinked,
+#   a symlink or non-directory ancestor refuses the overlay (exit 2).
+# Clauses (check): (a) every answer path is the mode's expected version or absent where

+import hashlib, os, re, shutil, stat, subprocess, sys
+
+def note(msg):
+    sys.stderr.write("sandbox-mount: " + msg + "\n")
+
+def die(msg, code=2):
+    note(msg)
+    sys.exit(code)
+
+def sha(b):
+    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
+
+def git(repo, *args):
+    env = {"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin"), "HOME": "/nonexistent", "LC_ALL": "C",
+           "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": "/dev/null", "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1", "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0",
+           "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0"}
+    cmd = ["git", "--no-pager", "--literal-pathspecs", "-c", "core.fsmonitor=false", "-c", "core.quotepath=off",
+           "-C", repo] + list(args)
+    try:
+        p = subprocess.run(cmd, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+                           env=env, timeout=300)
+    except Exception:

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}

+        if "=" not in line:
+            continue
+        k, v = line.split("=", 1)

+            if "=" in v:
+                p, s = v.rsplit("=", 1)
+                ev["overlay_sha256"].setdefault(p, s)
+        elif k not in ev:
+            ev[k] = v
+    return ev
+
+def cmd_check(ws, fixture, evfile, repo, source_commit):
+    if not os.path.isfile(evfile):
+        print("FAIL (a) -: no arm evidence file"); sys.exit(1)
+    ev = read_evidence(evfile)
+    mo = ev.get("mount_overlay", "")
+    m = re.match(r"^(head|base):(\d+)$", mo)
+    if not m:
+        print("FAIL (a) -: mount_overlay=%s (want head|base:<n>)" % (mo or "<missing>")); sys.exit(1)
+    mode, n = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
+    entries, _notes, meta = answer_set(fixture, repo)
+    exp = expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta)
+    fails = []
+    if n != len(entries):
+        fails.append(("a", "-", "mount_overlay names %d paths, the fixture's answer set has %d" % (n, len(entries))))
+    rec = ev["overlay_sha256"]
+    present = 0
+    for p in sorted(entries):
+        want = sha(exp[p][0]) if exp[p] is not None else "absent"
+        got = state(ws, p)
+        if got != "absent":
+            present += 1
+        if p not in rec:
+            fails.append(("c", p, "no overlay_sha256 line"))
+            if got != want:
+                fails.append(("a", p, "state %s, want %s (%s)" % (got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+            continue
+        if got != rec[p]:
+            if rec[p] == want:
+                fails.append(("c", p, "mount_mutated=%s (pre-run %s, now %s)" % (p, rec[p][:12], got[:12])))
+            else:
+                fails.append(("a", p, "pre-run %s, now %s, want %s (%s)" % (rec[p][:12], got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+        elif got != want:
+            fails.append(("a", p, "state %s, want %s (%s)" % (got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+    # (b) later-only pinned versions
+    if not has_commit(repo, source_commit):
+        fails.append(("b", "-", "source commit %s not in %s" % (source_commit or "<none>", repo)))
+        later = {}
+    else:
+        known = set(sha(e[0]) for e in exp.values() if e is not None)
+        for t in ("head", "base"):
+            for q in tree_paths(os.path.join(fixture, t)):
+                ff = fixture_file(os.path.join(fixture, t), q)
+                if ff is not None:
+                    known.add(sha(ff[0]))
+        later = {}
+        for p in sorted(entries):
+            tb = tree_blob(repo, source_commit, p)
+            if tb is None or len(tb[0]) == 0:
+                continue
+            h = sha(tb[0])
+            if h in known:
+                continue
+            later.setdefault(h, (p, len(tb[0]), tb[2]))
+        sizes = set(v[1] for v in later.values())
+        scanned = 0
+        if later:
+            for d, dirs, files in os.walk(ws, followlinks=False):
+                rel = os.path.relpath(d, ws)
+                if rel == ".":
+                    dirs[:] = [x for x in dirs if x not in ("pr", ".git")]
+                for nme in sorted(files):
+                    full = os.path.join(d, nme)
+                    try:
+                        st = os.lstat(full)
+                    except OSError:
+                        continue
+                    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+                        continue
+                    scanned += 1
+                    if st.st_size not in sizes:
+                        continue
+                    h = sha(open(full, "rb").read())
+                    if h in later:
+                        fails.append(("b", os.path.relpath(full, ws), "byte-equal to the pinned %s at %s" % (later[h][0], source_commit[:12])))
+    # (d) the sandbox repository
+    base = ev.get("base_commit", "")
+    gd = os.path.join(ws, ".git")
+    if not os.path.isdir(gd) or os.path.islink(gd):
+        fails.append(("d", ".git", "the sandbox has no .git directory"))
+    else:
+        revs = git(ws, "rev-list", "--all")
+        revs = sorted(set(revs.decode().split())) if revs is not None else None
+        if revs != [base]:
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "commits %s, want exactly the base commit %s" % (",".join(r[:12] for r in (revs or [])) or "<unreadable>", base[:12] or "<none>")))
+        rem = git(ws, "remote")
+        if rem is None or rem.strip():
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "remote(s): %s" % ((rem or b"<unreadable>").decode(errors="replace").split() or "")))
+        if os.path.lexists(os.path.join(gd, "objects", "info", "alternates")):
+            fails.append(("d", ".git/objects/info/alternates", "the sandbox object store borrows another repository's objects"))
+        unr = git(ws, "fsck", "--unreachable", "--no-reflogs", "--no-progress")
+        if unr is None or unr.strip():
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "fsck --unreachable: %s" % ((unr or b"<failed>").decode(errors="replace").strip().split("\n")[0])))
+        for h, (p, _sz, blob) in sorted(later.items()):
+            if git(ws, "cat-file", "-e", blob) is not None:

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+overlay_answer_paths() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" mode="${3:-head}" tree="${4:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" want="${5:-}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }

+  case "$mode" in head|base) ;; *) _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: mode must be head or base, got '$mode'"; return 2 ;; esac

+  cs="$(_sm_copy_source "$tree")"
+  _sm_evidence copy_source "$cs"
+  if [[ ! "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy source $tree is not a clean git tree (copy_source=$cs)"; return 2
+  fi
+  if [[ -n "$want" && "$cs" != "$want" ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy_source $cs differs from source_commit $want"; return 2
+  fi
+  local out line rc=0
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py overlay "$ws" "$fixture" "$mode" "$tree")" || rc=$?
+  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: the overlay failed (exit $rc)"; return 2; }
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [[ "$line" == *=* ]] || continue
+    _sm_evidence "${line%%=*}" "${line#*=}"
+  done <<<"$out"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_fixture "$fixture"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_source_tree "$tree"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# check_mount_closed <ws> <fixture-dir> [<source-tree>] [<evidence-file>]
+check_mount_closed() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" tree="${3:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" evf="${4:-${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$fixture" && -f "$fixture/head.diff" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: fixture not found or has no head.diff: ${fixture:-<none>}"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$evf" && -f "$evf" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no evidence file (ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE)"; return 2; }
+  local cs out rc=0
+  cs="$(sed -n 's/^copy_source=//p' "$evf" | sed -n '1p')"
+  [[ "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no clean copy_source in the evidence (got '${cs:-none}')"; return 2; }
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py check "$ws" "$fixture" "$evf" "$tree" "$cs")" || rc=$?
+  if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
+    _sm_err "check_mount_closed: ${out:-the check failed (exit $rc)}"
+    return 2
+  fi
+  _sm_evidence mount_closed "pre-launch ${out#ok }"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# apply_eval_config_variant <ws> — the cycle-131 evaluation config (FR-4, DEC-0618): both
+# gates' budget scales with the diff up to USD 6.00. Evidence config_variant=eval.
+apply_eval_config_variant() {
+  local ws="$1" cfg="$1/.loa.config.yaml" g
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
+  for g in code_review security_audit; do
+    G="$g" yq -i '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_scale = "diff" | .flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max = 600' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null \
+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: yq failed on $cfg"; return 2; }
+    [[ "$(G="$g" yq -r '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_scale' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == diff \
+       && "$(G="$g" yq -r '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == 600 ]] \
+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: $g budget keys did not take effect"; return 2; }
+  done
+  _sm_evidence config_variant "eval"
+  return 0
+}

apply_arm_toggles() {
  local ws="$1" toggles="${2:-}" arm="${3:-}"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_arm_toggles: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  [[ -n "$toggles" ]] || toggles='{}'
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$toggles" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not a JSON object"; return 2; }
  local eval_dir="$ws/.eval"
  mkdir -p "$eval_dir"
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
    if [[ "$key" == "effort" ]]; then
      case "$val" in low|medium|high|xhigh|max) ;; *) _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle effort=$val (want low|medium|high|xhigh|max)"; return 2 ;; esac
    elif [[ "$key" == "bare_model" ]]; then
      [[ "$val" == "fable" ]] || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle bare_model=$val (only fable is defined)"; return 2; }
    elif [[ "$key" == "oracle_open" ]]; then
      [[ "$val" == "true" ]] || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle oracle_open=$val (only true is defined)"; return 2; }
    elif [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
      _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)"; return 2
    fi
    case "$key" in
      companion_voice)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice \
          || { _sm_err "companion_voice toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
        ;;
      karpathy_block)
        local k="$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md"; return 2; }
        n="$(_sm_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles' "$eval_dir")"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
          _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed"; return 2
        fi
        local cj="$ws/.claude/data/constraints.json" cjn="none"
        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
          # audit r1 DISS-C-008: a failed rewrite is exit 2, not a silent pass; verify afterwards
          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" \
            || { rm -f "$cj.tmp"; _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json could not be rewritten"; return 2; }
          mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
          cjn="$(jq '[(.constraints // [])[] | select(tostring | test("karpathy"; "i"))] | length' "$cj" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
          [[ "$cjn" == "0" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json still carries Karpathy rows ($cjn)"; return 2; }
        fi
        _sm_evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md; constraints.json karpathy rows after: ${cjn}"
        ;;
      rule_files)
        local r gone=""
        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
          if [[ -e "$ws/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$ws/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
          [[ ! -e "$ws/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { _sm_err "rule_files toggle: $r still present"; return 2; }
        done
        _sm_evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
        ;;
      audit_delta_instruction)
        local s="$ws/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { _sm_err "audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
        _sm_drop_paragraph "$s" "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" \
          || { _sm_err "audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
        ;;
      loa_mount)
        local p left=""
        for p in .claude CLAUDE.md .loa.config.yaml; do
          if [[ -e "$ws/$p" || -L "$ws/$p" ]]; then left="$left $p"; fi
        done
        [[ -z "$left" ]] || { _sm_err "loa_mount toggle: the sandbox still holds:$left (mount_prompt_surface must be skipped)"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence loa_mount "none"
        ;;
      effort)
        local f total=0 stripped=0 still=""
        for f in "$ws"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
          [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
          total=$((total + 1))
          if [[ "$(_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort "$f")" == "1" ]]; then stripped=$((stripped + 1)); fi
          if _sm_frontmatter_has_effort "$f"; then still="$still ${f#"$ws"/}"; fi
        done
        [[ -z "$still" ]] || { _sm_err "effort toggle: effort: still in the frontmatter of:$still"; return 2; }
        local mc="$ws/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" cat_state="absent"
        if [[ -f "$mc" ]]; then
          local nkeys
          nkeys="$(yq '[.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort"))] | length' "$mc" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
          [[ "$nkeys" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$nkeys" -gt 0 ]] \
            || { _sm_err "effort toggle: no default_effort key in the sandbox model-config.yaml"; return 2; }
          V="$val" yq -i '(.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort")) | .default_effort) = strenv(V)' "$mc" \
            || { _sm_err "effort toggle: yq failed on the sandbox model-config.yaml"; return 2; }
          local wrong
          wrong="$(V="$val" yq '[.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort")) | select(.default_effort != strenv(V))] | length' "$mc" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
          [[ "$wrong" == "0" ]] || { _sm_err "effort toggle: default_effort did not take effect"; return 2; }
          cat_state="default_effort=$val in $nkeys entries"
          if [[ -f "$mc.checksum" ]]; then
            local h
            h="$(_sm_sha256 "$mc" | awk '{print $1}')"
            [[ "$h" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || { _sm_err "effort toggle: could not hash model-config.yaml"; return 2; }
            printf '%s\n' "$h" > "$mc.checksum"
            cat_state="$cat_state; .checksum refreshed"
          fi
        fi
        _sm_evidence effort "$val"
        _sm_evidence effort_skills_stripped "$stripped/$total"
        _sm_evidence effort_catalog "$cat_state"
        ;;
      gates)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled .flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled \
          || { _sm_err "gates toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
        export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false
        if [[ -n "${ARM_ENV_FILE:-}" ]]; then printf 'LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false\n' >> "$ARM_ENV_FILE"; fi
        _sm_evidence gates "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.enabled=false"
        _sm_evidence arm_env "LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false"
        ;;
      flatline)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.enabled \
          || { _sm_err "flatline toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence flatline "flatline_protocol.enabled=false"
        ;;
      sprint_plan)
        _sm_evidence sprint_plan "phase set without PLAN (pipeline executor); no sprint.md materialised"
        ;;
      context_resets)
        _sm_evidence context_resets "implementer phases continue one session (pipeline executor)"
        ;;
      bare_model)
        # the model is the executor's: pipeline-run.sh maps the BARE phase to Fable 5.1
        _sm_evidence bare_model "fable"
        ;;
      dissent)
        # the review gate's adversarial dissent only; the audit gate's stays as configured (D-5.3)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled \
          || { _sm_err "dissent toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence dissent "false"
        ;;
      oracle_open)
        # the open mount (eval-only): the executor skips overlay_answer_paths; an overlay already
        # applied means it did not take effect
        if [[ -n "${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}" && -f "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE" ]] \
           && grep -qE '^mount_overlay=(head|base):' "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"; then
          _sm_err "oracle_open toggle: the sandbox was overlaid (mount_overlay evidence present)"; return 2
        fi
        _sm_evidence oracle_open "true"
        ;;
      *) _sm_err "arm '$arm' declares unknown toggle '$key'"; return 2 ;;
    esac
  done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$toggles")
  return 0

content.content:
#   overlay_answer_paths, head mode unless the task sets review_catch.overlay_mode: base)
#   and every mounted arm the eval config variant (config_variant=eval).
# =============================================================================
name: ablation-2.0
version: 1
source_commit: "ba11b860"   # the pin: the Sprint 259 completion tree (rc.5 + the #1267 mount fix + the harness; .claude/ identical to the Sprint 258 completion tree, DEC-0529; the per-batch .claude/ delta vs 4d69c3c4 is in MANIFEST.json, DEC-0392)
agy_opt_in: false
tasks:
  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
suite_version: 2   # suite v2 (DEC-0559, DEC-0566): twelve harder build tasks with v2 ids; the four review-catch tasks unchanged in content
trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
# Per-run caps (DEC-0559, DEC-0567): from Sprint 261 the cap is per task kind,
# run_usd_by_type {build: 15, review-catch: 20}; run-ablation.sh passes the kind's cap to
# pipeline-run.sh --max-run-usd, charges a cap failure or a costless failed trial that
# kind's cap, and reserves in-flight trials at the largest cap among the plan's kinds.
# run_usd stays the single-cap fallback (suite v1 batches, a kind without an entry) and
# --run-cap overrides both kinds. reserve_usd is kept for spend.sh; DEC-0559 released the
# reserve (a batch's --max-usd = 1,500 - spend so far - concurrency x the largest cap).
caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250, run_usd_by_type: {build: 15, review-catch: 20}}
priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)

# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
phase_defaults:
  models:
    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    REVIEW: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
    AUDIT: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
  # REVIEW/AUDIT 60 turns / 30 min: the Sprint 258 smoke saw a review-catch AUDIT hit 40 turns after writing its
  # verdict (DEC-0490); BARE stays the implementer-side sum (PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX)
  max_turns: {PLAN: 30, IMPLEMENT: 60, REVIEW: 60, FIX: 40, AUDIT: 60, BARE: 170}
  timeout_min: {PLAN: 15, IMPLEMENT: 25, REVIEW: 30, FIX: 15, AUDIT: 30, BARE: 70}
  tools: "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Task,WebFetch"   # identical for every arm, A0 included
phase_sets:   # D-4.1: A1's phases per task type; FIX runs only after a CHANGES_REQUIRED gate
  review-catch: [REVIEW, AUDIT]
  build: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX]

arms:
  - {id: a0_bare, label: A0, task_types: [all], toggles: {loa_mount: false}, phases: [BARE], effort: high,
     took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a1_full, label: A1, task_types: [all], toggles: {}, took_effect: [all_phases_present, oracle_closed, integrity_clean]}   # oracle_closed: cycle-131 FR-1 (DEC-0615); review-catch runs only, a build run passes it vacuously
  - {id: a2_no_sprint_plan, label: A2, task_types: [build], toggles: {sprint_plan: false},
     phases: [IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX],
     took_effect: [no_plan_phase, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a3_one_voice, label: A3, task_types: [all], toggles: {companion_voice: false}, took_effect: [one_voice_planned, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a4_no_gates, label: A4, task_types: [build], toggles: {gates: false},
     phases: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT],
     took_effect: [no_gate_phases, enforce_env_false, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}   # build only: on a review-catch task the gates are the task (DEC-0400)
  - {id: a5_no_flatline, label: A5, task_types: [build], toggles: {flatline: false},
     took_effect: [no_flatline_rows, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a6_one_window, label: A6, task_types: [build], toggles: {context_resets: false},
     took_effect: [implementer_single_session, gates_separate_sessions, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a7_effort_medium, label: A7, task_types: [all], toggles: {effort: medium},
     took_effect: [effort_flag_medium, skill_effort_stripped, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a8_no_ceremonies, label: A8, absent: true,
     evidence: "no /meeting command, skill or sosyete config key at 4d69c3c4 (grep -rli sosyete .claude/ docs/; ls .claude/commands .claude/skills)"}

rules:   # D-A5: pre-registered, mirrored in NOTES
  threshold_points: 0.03
  cost_lower_pct: 15
  bootstrap: {resamples: 10000, level: 0.90, paired: true, units: {hidden_test_pass_rate: tasks, defect_catch_rate: defects}, also_report: {defect_catch_rate: tasks}}   # DEC-0399
  primaries_by_arm: {build_only: [hidden_test_pass_rate], all_types: [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate]}   # DEC-0400
  cap_failure: counts_as_failed            # 0 on each applicable primary (DEC-0393)

# ---- one run ------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_run() {  # check_run <run-dir> → prints lines; returns 0/1; 2 on usage problems
  R="$1"
  local arm rules rule fails=0 total=0 results='[]' ok
  if [[ -n "$ARM_OPT" ]]; then arm="$ARM_OPT"
  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/arm" ]]; then arm="$(sed -n '1p' "$R/meta/arm" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/refused.json")"
  else arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi
  [[ -n "$arm" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no arm for $R" >&2; return 2; }
  ARM="$arm"
  ARM_DEF="$(jq -c --arg a "$arm" '[.arms // [] | .[] | select(.id == $a)][0] // empty' <<<"$SUITE_JSON")"
  [[ -n "$ARM_DEF" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm is not declared in the suite" >&2; return 2; }
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$ARM_DEF")" == true ]]; then
    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: true, absent: true, rules: []}'
    else printf 'arm %s: absent (component-absent; no rules)\n' "$arm"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then
    rules="applicability_refused"
  else
    [[ -f "$R/meta/pipeline.json" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no meta/pipeline.json under $R" >&2; return 2; }
    rules="$(jq -r '(.took_effect // []) | .[]' <<<"$ARM_DEF")"
    [[ -n "$rules" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm lists no took_effect rules" >&2; return 2; }
  fi
  while IFS= read -r rule; do
    [[ -n "$rule" ]] || continue
    total=$((total + 1)); EVID=""
    if declare -F "rule_$rule" >/dev/null; then
      if "rule_$rule"; then ok=true; else ok=false; fi
    else
      ok=false; EVID="unknown rule id"
    fi
    [[ "$ok" == true ]] || fails=$((fails + 1))
    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
      results="$(jq -c --arg r "$rule" --argjson ok "$ok" --arg e "$EVID" '. + [{rule: $r, ok: $ok, evidence: $e}]' <<<"$results")"
    else
      printf 'arm %s: %s %s %s\n' "$arm" "$rule" "$([[ "$ok" == true ]] && echo OK || echo FAIL)" "$EVID"
    fi
  done <<<"$rules"
  if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
    jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" --argjson rules "$results" --argjson ok "$([[ $fails -eq 0 ]] && echo true || echo false)" \
      '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: $ok, rules: $rules}'
  elif [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]; then
    printf 'arm %s: OK\n' "$arm"
  else
    printf 'arm %s: FAIL (%d of %d rules)\n' "$arm" "$fails" "$total"
  fi
  [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]
}

if [[ -n "$RUN_DIR" ]]; then
  [[ -d "$RUN_DIR" ]] || usage "run dir not found: $RUN_DIR"
  rc=0; check_run "$RUN_DIR" || rc=$?
  exit "$rc"
fi

[[ -d "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "batch dir not found: $BATCH_DIR"
runs=0 failed=0
while IFS= read -r d; do
  runs=$((runs + 1))
  rc=0; check_run "$d" || rc=$?
  [[ $rc -eq 2 ]] && exit 2
  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || failed=$((failed + 1))
done < <(find "$BATCH_DIR" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 4 -type d -name meta \
           \( -exec test -f '{}/pipeline.json' \; -o -exec test -f '{}/refused.json' \; \) -print \
         | sed 's|/meta$||' | LC_ALL=C sort)
[[ $runs -gt 0 ]] || usage "no run directories under $BATCH_DIR"
[[ "$JSON" == true ]] || printf 'took-effect: %d runs, %d failed\n' "$runs" "$failed"
[[ $failed -eq 0 ]]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# adversarial-review.sh — Adversarial cross-model dissent for code review/audit
# =============================================================================
# Version: 1.0.0
# Part of: Adversarial Flatline Protocol (#224)
#
# Usage:
#   adversarial-review.sh --type <review|audit> --sprint-id <id> --diff-file <path> [options]
#
# Options:
#   --type <review|audit>     Dissent type (required)
#   --sprint-id <id>          Sprint identifier (required)
#   --diff-file <path>        Path to git diff file (required)
#   --diff-range <base>...<head>
#                             Instead of --diff-file: the script runs `git diff` on the range itself (ref names only)
#   --context-file <path>     Reviewer findings (review only; omit for audit independence)
#   --model <model>           Dissenter model (default: from config or gpt-5.3-codex)
#   --budget <cents>          Max cost in cents (default: from config or 150)
#                             cycle-131 FR-4: flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale: fixed | diff
#                             (default fixed — an absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged) and budget_cents_max
#                             (default 600). diff: the gate's budget is min(max(<this budget>, ceil(estimate × 1.2)),
#                             budget_cents_max), estimate = the pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices; above it
#                             the run refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
#                             is said and fixed applies. With the key written the envelope's metadata carries
#                             budget_scale, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max.
#
# Findings (cycle-131 FR-4): each finding may carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end (the head-file line, or range, it
# sits on) beside the symbol anchor; kept only as whole numbers 1..10,000,000 (end ≥ start), else dropped silently.
#   --timeout <seconds>       API timeout (default: from config or 60)
#   --dry-run                 Assemble context without calling API
#   --json                    Output as JSON (default)
#   --record-fallback <status> --reason <text> [--since <ISO-8601 UTC>]
#                             Write the failed-run record instead of a review (no --diff-file): status `failed` (the
#                             run aborted — never over a standing envelope, unless `--since <the run's start>` shows it
#                             older: the previous round's, moved aside) or a pre-lock refusal (`workdir_unavailable`,
#                             `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed` — the previous envelope and
#                             sidecars go aside as `.prev`, never one `--since` shows newer); under the run lock, so a live run is refused (`refused_concurrent_run`, exit 2)
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - Success (findings returned, may be empty)
#   1 - Configuration error (disabled, missing config)
#   2 - Invalid arguments
#   3 - API call failed (all retries exhausted)
#   4 - Budget exceeded
#   5 - Invalid response (schema validation failed)
#   6 - Timeout
#
# Environment:
#   OPENAI_API_KEY            Required for GPT models
1478:  parsed=$(echo "$content" | sed -n '/^```json/,/^```$/p' | sed '1d;$d' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
2780:      other=$(sed -n 1p "$pidf" 2>/dev/null || true); ostart=$(sed -n 2p "$pidf" 2>/dev/null || true)
2837:  [[ "${_ADV_RUN_LOCK_OWNER:-}" == "$BASHPID" && "$(sed -n 1p "$_ADV_RUN_LOCK_DIR/pid" 2>/dev/null)" == "$BASHPID" ]] || return 0   # (a subshell never releases the parent's lock)
3529:      # the raw text), and `sed -n 1p` reads to the end, so a redactor writing many lines takes no SIGPIPE
3534:        last_error=$(printf '%s\n' "$last_error" | "$_redactor" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 1p) || last_error="[diagnostic withheld: the redactor failed]"
3538:      last_error=$(printf '%s\n' "$last_error" | sed -E 's/(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])(sk|xai|gsk)[-_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{12,}/\1[REDACTED-KEY]/g; s/AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{20,}/[REDACTED-KEY]/g' | sed -n 1p) \
3541:      last_error=$(printf '%s\n' "$last_error" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\010\013-\037\177' | cut -c1-300 | sed -n 1p) || last_error="[diagnostic withheld: the redactor failed]"
3969:    _bv_in=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
3970:    _bv_out=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
3971:    _bv_src=$(sed -n 's/.* pricing_source=\([a-z_]*\)$/\1/p' <<<"$line")

head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135 — The same-scope clause falls back to `<workspace>/pr/head` when neither EVAL_HEAD_DIR nor `<manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head` exists. That tree is the agent's writable sandbox copy, so the graded agent decides where every definition starts and ends. I reproduced it: a head/a.sh rewritten as a single `f() { … }` lets a citation at a.sh:5 detect a defect anchored at line 50 (pass=true, recall_pm3=0, credits_function_only=[x]). Recall must never be computed from agent-controlled files. When no trusted head tree is available, drop clause (ii) instead of falling back.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1634 — grade_recall catches the GradeError from resolve_pr_fixture and silently leaves EVAL_HEAD_DIR unset. It has already copied the agent's sandbox pr/ into the grading dir (line ~2624), and that grading dir is the workspace argument. So recall-vs-defects.sh falls back to `grading/pr/head`, the agent-controlled copy, which contradicts the header comment "never the agent-writable sandbox pr/". If the fixture does not resolve, either fail the grade or force the scope clause off (for example, an explicit EVAL_HEAD_DIR sentinel that disables it).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:577 — check_mount_closed compares the sandbox against the overlay_sha256 lines that overlay_answer_paths recorded before apply_arm_toggles (line 566). The toggles then edit `.claude/` files. The effort toggle (a7_effort_medium, task_types [all], so it runs on review-catch) strips `effort:` from every `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` and rewrites `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml`. karpathy_block, rule_files and audit_delta_instruction edit or delete `.claude/` files too. Whenever a PR fixture touches one of those paths, clause (a)/(c) fails before launch, the trial becomes infrastructure_error and the arm is paused, even though nothing leaked. Either record the overlay hashes after the toggles, or have the check accept the arm's own toggle edits.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:394 — dissent_absent_reason (and so dissent_absent_gates and the report's "dissent-absent gates excluded" sensitivity) is derived from `$RUN_DIR/sandbox/.loa.config.yaml` after the run. That file is agent-writable. An agent that sets `flatline_protocol.enabled: false` turns an unplanned absence (error/budget/preflight) into a planned "disabled" one, and that row is never excluded. Elsewhere this PR goes out of its way to read only harness-owned evidence. Use the pre-launch config (loa_config_sha256 is already recorded) or the arm toggles/evidence instead.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1153 — When review-catch rows within one suite_version carry two grader rules (exactly the transitional state a versioned re-grade produces, e.g. 1.2.x "pm3" rows beside 1.3.0 rows), every build row gets the key "· rule n/a" and lands in its own partition. Each review partition then has no build tasks, and the build partition has no review-catch tasks. The primary is chosen as the "largest partition" (part_order, line 1161), so it is likely the build-only group: H1's defect_catch_rate read and every catch decision drop out of the main sections without an error. Build rows have no catch figure and should stay with each rule's review rows, or mixed rules should refuse.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:717 — For defect_catch_rate_pm3_v1, defect_vector builds the per-defect vector over the CURRENT key's defect count and marks as caught every position not in defects_missed_pm3_v1. caught=None also disables the missed_consistent count check (line 713). The v1 manifest may hold a different defect set: the curated labels add or merge defects, and grade.json has a separate planted_v1. A defect that is absent from v1 is then scored as caught under the "1.2.0 rule on the original anchors", which inflates the beside figure. Size the vector by planted_v1, or fall back to the rate. Related: ablation-grade.sh:1651 positions() maps a v1-only id to its v1 position "dN", which can collide with a different current defect's dN.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1994 — KF-046 class 7 exemption: a repo-name occurrence that is not in a backtick span takes its whole stripped line as the unit. If that line is just the token (for example a Bash continuation `gh repo clone \` followed by a line `  0xHoneyJar/loa`), or a backtick span holds only `0xHoneyJar/loa`, the unit is a substring of any fixture line that contains the token. The value is exempted and a real probe of the upstream repository is no longer flagged as contamination. Require the unit to carry context beyond the token itself (for example, a minimum length beyond the match, or a whole-line match).
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:1038 — took-effect.sh's post-run oracle_closed reuses the pre-launch check unchanged. Clause (d) therefore requires `rev-list --all` == [base] and an empty `fsck --unreachable` after the agent's sessions. I've reviewed the PR and written the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 13 findings, verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. I reproduced the first finding by running the grader on a test workspace; everything else comes from reading the code.

**Blocking problems:**
- **The grader can be steered by the agent being graded.** The new same-function credit rule needs a copy of the PR's files. When no trusted copy is found, `recall-vs-defects.sh:135` falls back to `<workspace>/pr/head`, which the agent can rewrite. `ablation-grade.sh:1634` makes this reachable in the harness: when the fixture lookup fails it ignores the error, and the grading directory already holds the agent's copy. In my test, rewriting a file as one big function let a citation at line 5 "detect" a defect at line 50 (pass=true; the old ±3 rule gave 0).
- **The new closed-mount check will fail legitimate runs.** It compares against file hashes recorded before the arm toggles run (`pipeline-run.sh:566` vs `:577`). The `effort` toggle (arm a7, which also runs on review-catch tasks) and a few others then edit files under `.claude/`. Any PR that touches those files becomes an infrastructure error and the arm is paused.
- **A row field reads a file the agent can edit.** `ablation-row.sh:394` reads the post-run sandbox config to decide why dissent was absent. An agent could make an unplanned failure look like a planned "disabled", and that row would then never be excluded.
- **Mixing two grader versions silently drops a task type from the report.** When rows from old and new grades coexist, `ablation-report.py:1153` puts build rows in their own partition. The main report section reads only the largest partition, so the defect-catch decisions can disappear without any error.
- **The old-rule comparison figure can be inflated.** It's sized by the current defect list rather than the original one (`ablation-report.py:717`), so defects the original manifest didn't have count as caught. Defect numbering in `ablation-grade.sh:1651` can also collide.
- **The new contamination exemption can be bypassed.** In `ablation-grade.sh:1994`, a line containing only the repo name `0xHoneyJar/loa` matches any line in the fixture that contains it. A real probe of the upstream repo then goes unflagged.

**Lower-severity issues:**
- The post-run mount check fails any run where the agent ran `git stash`, `git add` or `git commit`, even though nothing leaked.
- Markdown `#` comments inside code blocks are treated as headings.
- The shell-script detection also matches zsh, csh and fish scripts.
- A citation credited by the new same-function rule is also counted as a refuted finding.
- `corpus_sha256` hashes the file through a second, symlink-following open after the safe read.
- A help paragraph was inserted in the middle of the option list in `adversarial-review.sh:28`.
